sections.body: The MAIN IDEA is what a paragraph is mostly about. The other sentences are DETAILS that support it.
The main idea is often in the first sentence (the topic sentence), but not always. Sometimes it's at the end, or not written at all.
Test: ask 'What is this mostly about?' Then check: do most sentences support your answer?

Example: 'Octopuses are amazing escape artists. They can squeeze through tiny gaps. They change colour to hide. Some even squirt ink.' Main idea: octopuses are good at escaping. Everything else is a detail.
An INFERENCE is working out something the writer doesn't say directly, using clues in the text.
Pick a paragraph from any book. Write its main idea in 10 words or fewer.

quiz.q: 'Bees are important for farming. They carry pollen between flowers. This helps fruit and vegetables grow. Without bees, many crops would struggle.' What is the main idea?
options: Bees are important for growing food
hints: What is the paragraph MOSTLY about?
One option is just a detail that supports the big idea.
In the octopus example, 'they change colour' was a detail and 'octopuses are good at escaping' was the main idea.
quiz.explain: Every sentence supports one idea: bees matter for growing food. 'Carrying pollen' is a supporting detail.

quiz.q: Which sentence is a DETAIL, not a main idea? Paragraph: 'Recycling helps the planet. It saves energy. It reduces rubbish in landfills.'
hints: Which sentence do the others support?
Two sentences give reasons. One sentence is the big claim.
In 'Exercise is good for you. It makes your heart stronger.', the second sentence is a detail.
quiz.explain: 'It saves energy' is one reason that supports the main idea: recycling helps the planet.

quiz.q: 'Maya looked at the dark clouds and grabbed her umbrella.' What can you INFER?
hints: What clue does the writer give?
'Tom yawned and rubbed his eyes.' We can infer Tom is tired, even though it doesn't say so. Use the clues the same way.
quiz.explain: Dark clouds plus an umbrella are clues that Maya expects rain, even though the text doesn't say it.
